bioprojects.title: Sequencing and de novo assembly of the complete genome of P. aeruginosa MPAO1*, the parental strain of the transposon mutant collection

description.comment: This is the parental strain of the transposon mutant library of the Pseudomonas aeruginosa MPAO1 strain (Jacobs, M.A. et al., 2003, PNAS 100:14339-14334), which is disseminated by the group of Prof. Dr. Colin Manoil (University of Washington, Seattle, USA). We have de novo assembled the complete genome in very high quality merging PacBio and Illumina MiSeq data. The genome sequence (and the transposon mutant collection) represent the starting point of the work of an international consortium on biofilm formation and antibiotics resistance. (https://netzwerke.bam.de/Netzwerke/Navigation/EN/Projects/BEAT-AMR/beat-amr.html)

description.comment: In recent years, with the increasing global antimicrobial resistance, phage therapy has emerged as one of the most promising alternatives to antibiotics. Numerous studies have reported the effectiveness and safety of phage therapy in treating multidrug-resistant bacterial infections. However, there is limited research on the relationship between the emergence of phage-resistant strains and clinical outcomes. In this study, we applied phage nebulization therapy to a patient with carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa lung infection. After 8 weeks of treatment with P. aeruginosa phages, the patient's sputum bacterial load decreased, overall inflammatory markers decreased, and lung effusion significantly reduced. During the treatment, a phage-resistant P. aeruginosa strain NPA13B was isolated. To investigate the relationship between the emergence of phage-resistant strains and clinical outcomes, we performed whole-genome sequencing analysis on the resistant strain and validated the effect of phage resistance on bacterial virulence using the Galleria mellonella larvae infection model. Our conclusion is that phage therapy against P. aeruginosa demonstrates positive effects in reducing the bacterial load and improving clinical symptoms in the lungs.
